review_text: The reason people book hotels for their time away from home is to have a roof over their heads and an opportunity to wash themselves. Motel One somehow almost failed both these basic tourist needs for us. Yes, “almost” is the key word here, but the mood and first impression were ruined. I’ll tell you my story. The day before our booking date I receive an email from booking.com saying my credit card is invalid (my bad, forgot to update it before the trip). It says that unless I updated it within 24 hours, my booking will be cancelled. No big deal, I update it within an hour after the email. In the app my status is changed to “booking confirmed” again. Guess what happened at the front desk? That’s right: they cancelled my damn booking. Absolutely not willing to help and looking at my CONFIRMED booking in the app he doesn’t even apologize. The only room available on the spot is business suite. It seems I don’t have another choice - I pay for business suite: this was about “almost no roof over my head”. What if I was a traveler on budget? What if I simply didn’t have enough money? Not their problem. Cherry on top to the check-in: it was towards midnight and THERE WAS A LINE for check-in. We waited for 25 minutes only to learn that we’ve been cancelled. Another cherry: they blamed Booking.com for not sending an email about cancellation (remember this, it’s important for later). What’s up with lines at midnight? I’ll tell you. The hotel is HUGE. It’s enormous. And only TWO people and the front desk. In our case they called a third one, but it was still 25+ minutes. For this very reason don’t expect special treatment (not even a smile!) because you are not special when there are hundreds of guests. The shower thing. One morning it turns they don’t have hot water. Just no hot water. For me this was strike two. No phones in the room so we go downstairs to ask. As expected, there are a lot of people waiting (in the line, of course) to be explained. Pipes, they say.
